weeks.title: Steady Attention
weeks.principle: Sort what is yours to direct from what is not.
weeks.overview: This week builds the habit of returning attention to choices, effort, and attitude when events feel noisy.

dailyPractices.heading: Learn
dailyPractices.instruction: Write two short lists: what you can influence today and what you cannot. Keep the first list visible.
dailyPractices.reflectionPrompt: Where did this distinction immediately lower tension?

dailyPractices.heading: Notice
dailyPractices.instruction: Each time plans shift, name one response that still belongs to you before reacting.
dailyPractices.reflectionPrompt: Which response was easiest to reclaim?

dailyPractices.heading: Practice
dailyPractices.instruction: Choose one irritation and rehearse a calmer next action instead of replaying the trigger.
dailyPractices.reflectionPrompt: What changed when you moved from complaint to action?

dailyPractices.heading: Apply
dailyPractices.instruction: Before an important conversation, decide your intention and one behavior you will keep no matter the outcome.
dailyPractices.reflectionPrompt: Did your intention hold under pressure?

dailyPractices.heading: Examine
dailyPractices.instruction: Review one moment you felt pulled by circumstances and identify the exact decision point you still had.
dailyPractices.reflectionPrompt: What signal helps you spot that decision point earlier?

dailyPractices.heading: Integrate
dailyPractices.instruction: Pick one recurring stressor and define a standing response you can repeat next time.
dailyPractices.reflectionPrompt: How does repetition make this feel more manageable?

dailyPractices.heading: Review
dailyPractices.instruction: Summarize this week in one sentence beginning with: My effort is best used on...
dailyPractices.reflectionPrompt: What will you carry into next week?

weeks.sourceNote: Inspired by classical Stoic distinctions about agency and response.

weeks.title: Clear Seeing
weeks.principle: Events arrive first; interpretations arrive after.
weeks.overview: This week trains a small pause between what happened and the story added to it.

dailyPractices.heading: Learn
dailyPractices.instruction: Take one concern and split it into facts versus interpretation in two columns.
dailyPractices.reflectionPrompt: Which part was assumption rather than fact?

dailyPractices.heading: Notice
dailyPractices.instruction: When emotion spikes, describe the moment in neutral terms before naming meaning.
dailyPractices.reflectionPrompt: How did neutral language affect your tone?

dailyPractices.heading: Practice
dailyPractices.instruction: Challenge one automatic conclusion by proposing two alternative explanations.
dailyPractices.reflectionPrompt: Which alternative proved most plausible?

dailyPractices.heading: Apply
dailyPractices.instruction: In a difficult exchange, ask one clarifying question before defending your position.
dailyPractices.reflectionPrompt: What did you learn by asking first?

dailyPractices.heading: Examine
dailyPractices.instruction: Revisit a strong reaction from this week and rewrite the event description with only observable details.
dailyPractices.reflectionPrompt: What became less certain after rewriting?

dailyPractices.heading: Integrate
dailyPractices.instruction: Create a personal cue phrase for tense moments: facts first, story second.
dailyPractices.reflectionPrompt: Where did the cue interrupt escalation?

dailyPractices.heading: Review
dailyPractices.instruction: Note one relationship that improved when you separated event from judgment.
dailyPractices.reflectionPrompt: How will you continue this pause next week?

weeks.sourceNote: Inspired by Stoic attention to impressions and assent.

weeks.title: Purposeful Action
weeks.principle: Choose actions by values, not by guaranteed results.
weeks.overview: This week emphasizes consistent conduct even when outcomes remain uncertain.

dailyPractices.heading: Learn
dailyPractices.instruction: Name one value you want to express this week and one concrete behavior that shows it.
dailyPractices.reflectionPrompt: Why does this value matter right now?

dailyPractices.heading: Notice
dailyPractices.instruction: Watch for moments where fear of results tempts you to avoid the right action.
dailyPractices.reflectionPrompt: What avoidance pattern appeared?

dailyPractices.heading: Practice
dailyPractices.instruction: Take one small value-aligned action that you have postponed.
dailyPractices.reflectionPrompt: How did action change your mindset?

dailyPractices.heading: Apply
dailyPractices.instruction: Before a task, define success as quality of effort and integrity of method.
dailyPractices.reflectionPrompt: Did your definition of success reduce pressure?

dailyPractices.heading: Examine
dailyPractices.instruction: Identify one choice where you optimized for approval over principle and rewrite your preferred response.
dailyPractices.reflectionPrompt: What would courageous consistency look like there?

dailyPractices.heading: Integrate
dailyPractices.instruction: Create a brief pre-action checklist: value, next step, and tone.
dailyPractices.reflectionPrompt: Which part of the checklist was most useful?

dailyPractices.heading: Review
dailyPractices.instruction: Describe one uncertain outcome you can now meet with steadier effort.
dailyPractices.reflectionPrompt: How will you practice value-first action tomorrow?

weeks.sourceNote: Inspired by Stoic emphasis on character and intentional conduct.
